name: Saint Orrin's Comet
desc: A hermit cloister on a comet, home to heretics who split from the Order of Ilun.

gm.feel: Ammonia ice, scorched wool and burnt toast, in tunnels melted through dirty ice that refreeze into new shapes every orbit. Where Ilun whispers, this place shouts: scarred, gleeful heretics argue in the corridors, sing badly at all hours and smell faintly of singed hair. Nothing's for sale until you've argued for it, because here you pay by being wrong out loud in front of everyone, and they'll take flour as well.

districts.name: The Disputation Pit
districts.desc: A scooped-out bowl of ice with a bench around it and a very old chalk line. Anyone may challenge anyone on anything, the crowd judges and the loser cooks.

districts.name: The Long Melt
districts.desc: Cells and tunnels melted into the comet by generations of heretics, a little different each time round. Hermits live at the far ends, and some have been arguing through the same wall for forty years.

districts.name: The Loft
districts.desc: A wire cage bolted to the surface, under the black sky and the long bright tail. One heretic is always up there, singing into the dark in shifts, and they've kept this up without a break for a thousand years.

districts.name: The Burn Ward
districts.desc: A warm low cave where singers who've stood too many shifts are looked after by the ones who haven't yet. Nobody's allowed to be alone in it, and it's full of terrible jokes.

districts.name: Orrin's Hole
districts.desc: A dry shaft in the ice where the lost testament of Saint Orrin was supposedly found. Pilgrims leave burned gloves here, and Mother Orsolya uses it to keep her beer cold.

complications: A surface jet opens under Cell Row, and the whole corridor begins to fill with fog and fast-moving gravel.
The singer on the Loft has collapsed, the relief is too burned to climb and everyone has turned to look at your party's Resonant.
An Inquisitor's cutter has appeared off the tail, and it's asking very politely for a list of residents.
You've lost an argument in the Pit in front of everyone, and you've got to cook dinner for the whole cloister with what's left of your stores.
The comet's orbit is carrying it closer in this year than it's been for centuries, and the Long Melt has begun to run with water.
One of your people has been talked into something by an expert, and they're delighted about it, and it can't be undone.
secrets: At twenty-four, to win an argument with Ione, Orsolya forged the lost testament of Saint Orrin in a weekend: the field isn't left over, it's still being made, and the Order is listening to the wrong end of it. She carried it to the comet, where a dwindling few were still singing, and found that it was true. She thinks that whatever's at the other end should be woken and asked, and she's told nobody.

The heretics are the only people still doing the job. Their rite is the old one, singing a shift of the watch, from the pages cut out of the Ilun Codex that Orsolya still holds. They lost the instrument that kept a singer in tune, so all of them burn. Orsolya tells her idiots that the burning is holy, and she knows it's an equipment failure. There are eleven left.

The fist-sized pale ring holding up the kitchen's soup pot is a gate_key, the relief crews' pass through the Pale Gate, stolen when the heretics fled. Orsolya knows exactly what it is. She also knows that a drinking blade began as a surgeon's tool for dragging a singer back, and it's why she laughs at Inquisitors.

encounters: Mother Orsolya interrupts your greeting with one word: "Wrong." She offers you a wager. If you can say what the Order of Ilun is for, in one sentence that she can't knock down inside a minute, she'll answer one question of yours. Her idiots have started taking bets, and they aren't giving you good odds.

A nineteen-year-old singer has been in the Loft for three days, because her relief can't climb. Someone needs to go up and hold her steady for an hour. Her hands are smoking gently inside her gloves. She looks at you through the wire and asks if you know any good jokes, and she means it.

A young novice from Ilun has been hiding in the Long Melt since the Fall. She was told to get up at a certain hour, with everyone in her priory, and walk out of the door. She didn't. She'd like to know whether Brother Cael is still looking for her, and she begs you not to tell him where she is.

A former Inquisitor's cadet has been living in the Long Melt, with a pale blade he can't bring himself to throw away. An old heretic turns the handle over in her burned fingers and starts to laugh. She says that it's Proctor's work, it was made for a nurse's grip, and he's been holding it the wrong way round. He looks ill. He asks you to make her stop, or to make her go on.

Orsolya gives you a folded scrap for Abbess Ione, as she's done with every traveler for fifty years. It's a reply to a letter that she won't admit she's had. You could read it. It's three words, and two of them are the same word. One of the idiots mentions that the last courier got eleven days' silence and a bag of herbs.

You're challenged in the Pit, in front of the entire cloister, to defend the claim that your fleet deserves to go on existing. If you win, they'll sing a shift for your sick and your sleepless, and it really does help. If you lose, it's your turn to do the latrines. The old woman has already started heckling, and you haven't opened your mouth.

A surface jet is about to open under a hermit's cell. He won't leave, since he's forty years into a vow of remaining in one room and arguing through the wall with his neighbor. The neighbor died nine years ago. The hermit's aware of that. He says the man's position has become much more interesting since then.

A cheerful trader in a battered shuttle is selling burn salve at ten times its price, and you recognize the crates as stock stolen from Anselm's Mercy. The heretics are paying him in lumps of carved pale stone from the old diggings. They have no idea what those are worth, and neither does he, and you do.

One of your crew has a touch of Resonance, and has been invited up to the Loft for a go. It's only five minutes, the heretics say, and it doesn't hurt until later. Your crewman comes to you looking happier than they've looked in six months. They've only come to you for permission out of politeness.

A dying heretic in the Burn Ward takes hold of your sleeve. She's stood eleven thousand hours, and she'd like you to write that down and see that it gets put in the book. Which book? She doesn't know. She was told by the one before her that there's a book, and that somebody keeps it. She wants to be sure she's on it.

The cook is the only person on the comet with no Resonance, a stout former Syndicate smuggler who came here to rob them, and stayed to feed them. He's the only one who knows how little food is left. He'd like you to stop letting them talk you into things, and to leave as much flour as you can, and he's crying as he says it.

Orsolya stops in the middle of an insult and coughs up a small quantity of smoke. Every idiot in the room falls silent. She grins at them, and says "Wrong", and it all starts up again. Late that night she finds you alone. She wants to know how long you think she's got, and if your ship could get her within shouting distance of Ilun.

A Choir Hunter has been sitting on the comet's crust for thirty years, facing outward. The heretics call it Brother Silver, and they set a place for it at table. It's never moved. It turns its head as your shuttle lands. Everyone in the cloister is thrilled, and they want to know what you've done to it.

Two heretics are holding a formal debate about whether you, personally, are real. It began as a joke. It's now in its second day, it's been very well attended and they'd like you to give evidence. One side has just cited something you've never told anyone.
rumors: "Wrong." That's the first thing she'll say to you. That's how you know she likes you. The second thing she says is also "Wrong", but with more teeth.
They set themselves on fire out there. I mean it. For a thousand years. You tell me what kind of a faith needs that.
The Order's been listening to the wrong end of it all this time. That's what Saint Orrin's testament says. I've read it, and it's very persuasive. It's got a lot of jokes in it, for a saint.
There's eleven of them left. There used to be thousands. I asked what happens when there's none, and she said, "Then nobody's on duty, you fool," as if that were a thing that made sense.
Those pages got cut out of the Ilun Codex for a reason. The Abbess says there was a fire. People who've had a fire don't generally use a ruler.
The comet's coming in close this time around, and that whole cloister's made of ice. I'd pay my respects soon, if I were you. They'd like that. They'd tell you that you were doing it wrong.
Inquisitors won't land there, not since that one walked into the Pit to arrest the old woman, and walked out four hours later and resigned.
There's a silver thing on the crust that they feed. Well, they put out a bowl. They'll tell you its name. They'll tell you it's a very good listener, unlike some abbesses they could mention.
An Orrin heretic can light a stove by insulting it. That sounds like a joke. I've seen it done.
Don't bet against the old woman in the Pit. Her own Order threw her out for winning.
You go up to the Loft a young fool, and you come down an old one with no eyebrows. I did it once, on a dare. It's the happiest I've ever been, and I'd advise you very strongly against it.

She and the Abbess have been writing to each other for fifty years, and not one letter's been longer than a line. I've carried a few. I don't know what they're saying. I know I'd hate to be in the middle of it.
The cook's got an old pale ring propping up the soup pot. He says it's getting heavier. I asked him why he doesn't just use something else, and he looked at me like I'd asked him to move the moon.
